**7B.8 Research Note**

Bottom line: the 2024 record looks mixed but not broadly opportunistic. Scholz repeatedly made public, rule-based explanations and backed formal processes, but there are also credible signs of evasiveness and a few transparency weak points around Cum-Ex/Warburg and sensitive security policy. I do not see strong evidence of systematic, self-serving manipulation of public information.

**Evidence leaning yes**
- [Bundesregierung / Taurus decision explanation](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-fr/service/archives/chancelier-questions-2024-2265010) | Bundesregierung | 4 Mar 2024 | Scholz openly explained the Taurus refusal as a boundary against German military involvement; this is direct evidence of stating a tradeoff publicly rather than concealing it. | QIDs: 7B.8; 7B.6
- [Bundestag / government questioning on Taurus](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2024/kw11-de-regierungsbefragung-991060) | Deutscher Bundestag | 13 Mar 2024 | Scholz repeated the Taurus rationale in the Bundestag, showing a willingness to put the decision on the record even amid opposition accusations of “half-truths.” | QIDs: 7B.8; 7B.6
- [Government budget and growth package](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/budget-2025-2298116) | Federal Government | 5 Jul 2024 | Scholz presented a negotiated 49-measure package and linked it to tax relief, infrastructure, social housing, and growth, which reads as formal policy-making rather than hidden reversal or manipulation. | QIDs: 7B.8; 7B.5
- [Public questioning at summer press conference](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/chancellor-summer-press-conference-2024-2301040) | Federal Government | 24 Jul 2024 | Scholz answered journalists’ questions at length in public, which supports a pattern of open explanation and post-decision scrutiny. | QIDs: 7B.8; 7B.6
- [Budget priorities and social support](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/service/newsletter-und-abos/bulletin/bundeskanzler-haushalt-2257440) | Bundesregierung | 31 Jan 2024 | Scholz tied the budget to Bürgergeld, Wohngeld, child benefit, and child supplement, which is evidence of committing to a stated social agenda through formal budget channels. | QIDs: 7B.8; 7B.5
- [AI Act compromise / rule-based regulation](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/germany-will-approve-eus-planned-ai-act--sources-3286730) | Reuters via Investing.com | 30 Jan 2024 | Reuters reported the government reached a compromise on the EU AI Act, suggesting formal rule-based bargaining rather than opportunistic or secretive reversal. | QIDs: 7B.8

**Evidence leaning no**
- [Coalition collapse after Lindner dismissal](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/explainergerman-coalition-collapses-what-comes-next-3706936) | Reuters via Investing.com | 6 Nov 2024 | Firing Lindner collapsed the coalition and triggered political chaos; this is strong evidence of broken coalition commitments and opportunistic crisis management, though not proof of private gain. | QIDs: 7B.8; 7B.5
- [Confidence vote and early elections](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2024/kw47-vertrauensfrage-1030198) | Deutscher Bundestag | 16 Dec 2024 | Scholz lost the confidence vote and moved through the constitutional path to elections; this supports formal rule-following, but the late-year breakdown still undercuts any simple claim of durable commitment keeping. | QIDs: 7B.8; 7B.6
- [Cum-Ex inquiry memory gaps](https://www.tagesschau.de/investigativ/ndr-wdr/cum-ex-scholz-untersuchungsausschuss-100.html) | tagesschau.de | 5 Dec 2024 | The report describes continuing unresolved questions and repeated “memory gaps,” which is credible evidence of evasive handling of a politically sensitive file. | QIDs: 7B.8; 7B.6
- [Warburg inquiry legal memo](https://www.tagesspiegel.de/politik/geheimes-kanzleramts-gutachten-in-cum-ex-affare-scholz-darf-weiter-in-deckung-bleiben-11756357.html) | Tagesspiegel | 4 Jun 2024 | Reporting suggested the Chancellery used a legal memo to blunt scrutiny of the Warburg affair, a concrete sign of trying to contain damaging information. | QIDs: 7B.8; 7B.7; 7B.6
- [5G security decision handled confidentially](https://www.onvista.de/news/2024/05-23-bericht-regierung-vertagt-entscheidung-ueber-strengere-vorschriften-im-5g-netz-0-20-26275293) | Reuters via onvista | 23 May 2024 | Sensitive 5G decisions were handled in confidential interministerial talks and ministries declined public comment, which is a transparency weak point even if it does not prove bad faith. | QIDs: 7B.8; 7B.7; 7B.6
- [BND surveillance ruling](https://www.bundesverfassungsgericht.de/SharedDocs/Pressemitteilungen/EN/2024/bvg24-093.html) | Bundesverfassungsgericht | 8 Nov 2024 | The Court found parts of the BND surveillance framework unconstitutional and oversight inadequate, which is structural evidence that accountability controls remained too weak in 2024. | QIDs: 7B.8; 7B.7; 7B.6

**Search gap**
- I did not find strong evidence that Scholz systematically lied about assets, donations, or campaign finance in 2024.
- The best negative evidence is narrower: coalition rupture, Cum-Ex/Warburg evasiveness, the possible Chancellery effort to contain scrutiny, and confidential handling of a few sensitive policy files.
- The best positive evidence is also narrower: he usually gave public reasons, accepted parliamentary and press scrutiny, and used formal bargaining and constitutional procedures rather than clandestine reversal.
